Area of Study 6: Innovations in Music 1900 to Present — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 6: Innovations in Music 1900 to Present brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: It is always C major.
The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
